title: Ukraine orders families with children to leave Pokrovsk as Russian forces approach
body:
On 19 August 2024 local authorities in Ukraine's Donetsk Oblast ordered families to leave the city of Pokrovsk and nearby towns and villages, starting the following day. Some residents left immediately by train and bus, and evacuees were offered shelter in western Ukraine. About 53,000 people still lived in Pokrovsk, according to officials.

Russian forces were about 6 miles from the outskirts of Pokrovsk, according to officials the previous week. Myrnohrad was less than 6 miles from the front line, and Selydove about 3 miles. The Institute for the Study of War estimated that Russian forces had advanced about 0.8 square miles per day in the Pokrovsk region over the previous six months. Ukrainian commander-in-chief Oleksandr Syrskyi said that heavy battles were under way near Pokrovsk and that Toretsk was under heavy pressure.

The Boston Globe, republishing an Associated Press report, described Pokrovsk as one of Ukraine's main defensive strongholds and a key logistics hub. It said that Russia had spent about six months attacking across Donetsk after taking Avdiivka. Ukraine's incursion into Kursk, begun on 6 August, was aimed in part at easing pressure in the east by forcing Moscow to divide its forces.
